messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED - capacity allocation anomaly (P1). Automated checks show cross-tier routing from dedicated-tagged traffic into hosted pools. Alert group: routing-policy-errors. Pager sent to oncall. Link: https://internal.redwood/incident/3032101234

alex: acknowledged, I'm taking this. Observing spike in 502/504s and model-variant mismatches. Triage in progress.

leo: customer-rep here — ACME reported degraded responses at ~12:09UTC, some responses returned smaller models unexpectedly. They've escalated to TPM.

maria: I'm seeing a config diff landed 03/14 by rollout-service that adjusted the capacity-tag evaluation order. Quick grep: 
```
policy.capacity_tag_eval:
  order: [region, tier, affinity]
  invert_on_mismatch: true  # <-- suspicious
```
The invert flag was added as part of an optimization.

alex: can you query how many requests matched dedicated-tier but routed to hosted pool?

maria: running quick query...
```
SELECT COUNT(*) AS misrouted, tenant_id
FROM request_logs
WHERE routed_pool = 'hosted' AND request_header['X-Capacity-Tier'] = 'dedicated'
  AND ts BETWEEN 3032100000 AND 3032104800
GROUP BY tenant_id
ORDER BY misrouted DESC
LIMIT 20;
```
Result: total misrouted ~ 4,960 requests. Top affected tenant: acme-inc (tenant_id=acme-42) ~4,200 requests.

alex: thanks. That's enough to justify immediate mitigation. Plan: 1) rollback routing policy change 2) add a temporary hard rule to block cross-tier routes 3) notify customer. Who can rollback?

maria: I can rollback the policy. Preparing rollback patch now. Will run a dry-run then apply.

sam: product/infra note — this impacts guaranteed isolation for Dedicated customers. Prioritize rollback. What's customer-visible impact?

leo: ACME saw ~1.1% of their requests fail with 5xx and ~3.7% returned a lower-capacity model (shorter responses). They opened case CS-12345.

alex: oncall-pagerduty: please mute noisy routing-policy-errors alert while we remediate. We still want the P1 notification to remain.

oncall-pagerduty: Muting alert channel routing-policy-errors for 30m per request from alex.

maria: applying rollback: 
```
# rollback config to commit abc123 (pre-change)
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood/configs/rollback -d '{"commit":"abc123", "component":"policy-engine"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```
Applying now.

maria: deployed rollback to staging, running canary. Logs look good. Pushing to prod in 2m.

alex: while rollback propagates, flip on temporary hard rule to prevent any request with header X-Capacity-Tier=dedicated from routing to hosted pools:
```
api> POST /admin/rules
{"name":"block-dedicated-to-hosted","priority":1000,"match":{"header.X-Capacity-Tier":"dedicated","target_pool":"hosted"},"action":"block","ttl":1800}
```
maria: rule applied. Verified via sampling: 100% of sampled dedicated-tagged requests now either route to dedicated or get rejected rather than go to hosted.

alex: good. Watch latency and error rates for 10m, then start lifting the block after rollback verified.

support-bot: Draft customer update prepared: 
"Hey ACME — we detected a routing policy regression that caused a subset of your dedicated requests to be served by hosted pools, resulting in degraded responses for a small portion of your traffic. We rolled back the routing change and applied a temporary safeguard; your traffic should be back to normal. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with a timeline and remediation.
— Redwood Support"

leo: sending to ACME now, marking case CS-12345 with interim update.

maria: rollback fully applied to prod at 3032104200. Running post-rollback verification.

alex: monitoring metrics: misrouted requests dropped to zero within 45s of rollback. Error rate for acme-inc back to baseline.

maria: removing the hard block and letting normal routing resume at 3032104620.

alex: summary so far — mitigation applied, rollback complete, hard guard removed. Next: capture timeline, logs, and open a postmortem. Assigning owners: maria for root cause analysis (config regression), alex for remediation plan and alerts tuning, sam for customer communication and SLA review.

sam: will prepare customer-facing postmortem and coordinate with ACME TPM. Also flagging contract impact review if needed.

maria: preliminary root cause: a boolean inversion in the new evaluation flag (invert_on_mismatch) caused the policy engine to flip tag matching logic for a limited rollout (10% of routes) — rollout rollout-service expanded percentage prematurely due to a feature gate bug. Patch ready to remove the failing flag and add unit tests.

alex: are there any remaining elevated alerts?

oncall-pagerduty: All noisy alerts for this incident are muted; routing-policy-errors alerts will remain suppressed until postmortem is filed.

support-bot: Customer update sent at 3032104720. ACME acknowledged and requested ETA on full RCA.

leo: ACME noted they saw visible degradation from 12:08–12:25UTC. We'll align our timeline with that window in the postmortem.

maria: creating PR to add regression test and revert the optimization flag permanently. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/policy-engine/pull/2974

alex: good work team. Closing active remediation. Please drop final notes into the incident tracker and start the postmortem template.

sam: assigning postmortem to SRE + Runtime Eng. Target draft in 48h.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — mitigation complete, rollback applied, postmortem required. Severity: P1 -> mitigated. Resolution timestamp: 3032104834. Impact: single enterprise (acme-inc), ~5k misrouted requests, customer-visible errors for ~1.1% of their traffic during window.

maria: adding follow-ups: harden rollout-service on percentage expansion, add canary webhook to prevent auto-increase without manual approval, add unit test for invert flag.

alex: logging handoff: oncall ends shift; followups owned by listed assignees. If any regression or customer escalation, reopen paging.

support-bot: Postmortem template created: https://docs.internal/incidents/3032101234-pm

leo: thanks all. I'll keep ACME looped in on progress.

sam: closing thread for incident communications.
